newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends higher, but resistance intact.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends higher, but resistance intact.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures posted strong gains on Thursday, ending just beneath session highs, but turnover was thin and prices failed to get past key technical levels, traders said.
A late-session push by speculators drove the most-active July contract to a high of $1,478 a tonne, just shy of resistance at $1,480 -- the bottom of a key overhead chart gap to $1,501, traders said.
July futures closed at $1,475, up $17 on the day, after sinking to a low of $1,456. Spot May gained $15, to $1,452, while the back months rose $16 to $18.

The market gapped some $10 a tonne higher at the opening and drifted in firmer territory for the bulk of the session, but with few fresh fundamentals to trade on, traders said interest was extremely light.
They noted, however, that the market typically slows down at this time of year.
"In April and May arrivals wind down," one trader said. "Consumption figures are all out for the first quarter. It's too early to look at pod counts. There's just not a heck of a lot to look at."
He said the market may have gotten some mild support by concerns that Ivorian shippers were having difficulty fulfilling nearby commitments.
Exporters and crop analysts in Abidjan said on Thursday Ivorian shippers with insufficient cocoa stocks to meet May contracts were facing a shortage of good quality export grade port arrivals.

In other news, heavy April rainfall in Ivorian cocoa-growing regions have favored mid-crop (May-Sept) pod growth and flowering for early 1997/98 main crop (Oct-April) harvests, weather and crop analyts said on Thursday.
Crop analysts' estimates of the 1996/97 midcrop range between 150,000 tonnes and 200,000 tonnes but rains into May will partly determine harvests. Arrivals stood at 970-980,000 tonnes by mid April.
Young flowers for 1997/98 main crop harvests where more abundant than at the same time last year but harvest estimates will not be possible until June onwards, analysts said.
An estimated 5,691 lots were traded on the day.
